algorithm_menu.name: Algorithm Menu
algorithm_menu.description: Three artifacts declare an axis called algorithm. grid2d lists 12 values, grid3d lists 8, profile lists 16 - and the union of all three is 36, because EVERY PAIRWISE INTERSECTION IS EMPTY. That is not a family sharing a vocabulary, it is three dispatch tables sharing a word: each member's _create_cartridge() is a match block over its own enum, one branch per preload, and each spelled its menu entry after its own cartridge file, so grid2d's BFS_FLOOD and grid3d's BFS are the same traversal and never collide. An axis is a dimension of variation; this is a switch statement. Eight of the thirty-six are rebuilt here on ONE substrate - a 33 x 33 relief of 1089 cells on a 0.96 m vertical panel - and the second axis, kind, names the thing that actually makes two of them comparable: whether the panel is a spacetime diagram (automaton), a graph (search), or a plotted function (signal). Every algorithm belongs to exactly one kind, so kind PARTITIONS algorithm rather than crossing it: 8 of the 24 cells are defined and the other 16 render the kind's bare substrate, which makes the emptiness visible instead of hidden. Four findings the code gave up that the brief did not have: RULE30, RULE110 and RULE90 are ONE cartridge at three values of rule_number: int, which ca_bridge separately declares as an axis named rule; SLOW and DISCO are one rule at two tempos and a palette; RANDOM is randi() % 8 every cell every step and its own header calls it the antithesis cartridge; and a THIRTEENTH enum member, DISCO, is invisible to check_dna_declarations because the comment above it contains a comma and the enum body is split on commas - the deriving tool and the gate are the same parser, so the gate says ok about a declaration that is missing one of the code's values. Deterministic from RNG_SEED 20260816, which is this bench's own because none of the three members declares a seed anywhere - they draw from the global generator with bare randf() and step under _process on a clock, so most values of this axis are a different picture on every boot and at every shutter. No randf outside a seeded generator, no noise, no _process, no Timer.
dev_themes: an axis that is a menu
the cross product that is mostly empty
interactions: stand at kind=automaton and walk the three rules: RULE30 fills a symmetric triangle 437 cells deep, RULE90 fills the same envelope with a Sierpinski gasket at 245, and RULE110 leans - 228 lit cells left of centre against 89 right, so its envelope is half a triangle. Three pictures, and in grid2d's own factory three calls to the SAME cartridge with 30, 110 and 90 passed to its constructor

put BFS_FLOOD and DIJKSTRA side by side at kind=search. Same 1089 cells, same 260 walls, same source, same 823 reachable cells. BFS draws diamond contours because every edge costs one hop; Dijkstra draws the same cone with wobbled contours because every edge costs something in [0.5, 1.5]. Set the weights to 1.0 and the two frames are one frame - which is what it means to say these are two entries in two different menus for one algorithm

then add DFS_MAZE, which is the third value of the same kind and is NOT a shortest path at all: it has no metric, only an order, so its relief is a snaking ribbon rather than a cone. That is the difference a kind can hold and a menu cannot

look at LOGISTIC_MAP at kind=signal and count the levels it uses. Six of thirty-three. The cartridge is named for the bifurcation diagram and averages 200 draws of the attractor at each r, which collapses the fan to its mean - a nearly flat line spanning 0.5195 to 0.6757 of its own declared y-range. Its own comment inside step() says a bifurcation diagram should show the last N values, and then averages anyway

walk any row across the kind axis - RULE30 at automaton, then at search, then at signal. Two of the three are the bare substrate, because a rule for a 1-D line is not defined on a graph or on a plotted function. Sixteen of the twenty-four cells are like that, and they are three images, not sixteen
algorithm_menu.capacity: SEE that a DNA axis can be a menu rather than a dimension - thirty-six values across three members with an empty intersection - and that the axis the family should have had is the one naming what KIND of thing each value is, which partitions the menu and leaves the cross product mostly empty

spatial_needs.footprint_note: THE STAGE IS THE FOOTPRINT AND IT IS DRAWN BEFORE EITHER AXIS IS CONSULTED: a 0.96 x 0.96 m panel 0.024 m thick standing on the floor, and four 0.030 m corner studs proud of its face by exactly D_MAX = 0.034 m at x, y = +-0.465. The studs are the reason the AABB is a constant. Without them the DEPTH of the box would be a fact about which kind was picked - a bare signal cell reaches only D_BODY 0.018 and a bare automaton cell only D_MAX at one single cell - the camera would move between cells, and every measured pair would carry a framing difference it did not earn. The FIGURE inside the stage moves a great deal: the drawn field is 0.84 x 0.84 m in every cell, but the cells not at D_OFF run from 1 of 1089 (bare automaton) through 245 (RULE90), 350 (RULE110), 437 (RULE30), 561 (SINE_WAVE), 699 (LOGISTIC_MAP) to 1083 (all three searches). The world box is 0.96 x 0.96 x 0.058 in every one of the twenty-four cells regardless. layout=ladder stands the eight native cells in a row at 1.10 m pitch, about 7.7 m wide, and is a design view rather than a map placement.

measurements.source: computed_from_geometry in a Python replica built from the same constants; no Godot was run. The box is the STAGE and nothing else: the panel spans x and y at +-0.48 about its own centre at y = 0.48, its back face sits at z = -PANEL_T = -0.024, and the proudest things in any cell are the four corner studs and the deepest cells, both reaching z = D_MAX = 0.034. Nothing either axis draws can exceed that: every cell is 0.019 m square and at most 0.034 m proud, and every cell is inside the 0.84 m field, which is 0.06 m inside the panel on every side.

dna.default: algorithm=RULE30, kind=automaton. RULE30 because IT IS THE FAMILY'S OWN DEFAULT RULE WRITTEN TWICE IN ONE FILE: cartridge_rule_1d.gd declares `var rule_number: int = 30` and then `func _init(rule: int = 30)`, so a bare .new() is rule 30, and it is also the first of the three that grid2d's factory constructs and the first value ca_bridge lists under its own `rule` axis. It is not any member's default ALGORITHM - grid2d ships GAME_OF_LIFE, grid3d ships BFS, profile ships SINE_WAVE - and it could not be, because those three defaults name three different kinds and only one of the three is even in this subset. THAT DISAGREEMENT IS ITSELF THE FINDING and is why the default is derived from the cartridge rather than from the menu. kind=automaton because it is the kind RULE30 belongs to: a default sitting in a foreign kind would ship the bench as a bare substrate, so every map placing it at default would show furniture rather than an argument. NOTE WHAT THE DEFAULT CELL COSTS: it is the densest and most symmetric of the three automata, so it is the flattering tile, and it is also the one whose difference from its two siblings the critic's own statistic cannot rank - see predicted_degeneracy for why the automaton kind saturates.
dna.note:
WHAT THE VALUES MEAN, where each word came from, and which member it came from. THE FAMILY FIRST, and it is a census before it is an argument: three artifacts declare an axis called `algorithm`, with 12, 8 and 16 values. THE UNION IS 36. Every pairwise intersection is EMPTY - grid2d against grid3d, grid2d against profile, grid3d against profile, all three measured, all three the empty set. cohort_bench's family agreed on five words out of five and that was the corpus's most unanimous vocabulary; this family agrees on nothing out of thirty-six, and it is the corpus's least. The near-misses are the tell rather than the exception: grid2d's BFS_FLOOD and grid3d's BFS are the same traversal, grid2d's DFS_MAZE and grid3d's DFS are the same traversal, and they fail to collide only because each member named its menu entry after its own cartridge file.

SO `algorithm` IS NOT AN AXIS. An axis is a dimension of variation - one thing varied while everything else is held. This is a DISPATCH TABLE: the list of cartridges a particular widget happens to preload. In all three members the mechanism is literally `_create_cartridge()`, a `match` block over the file's own enum with one `preload(...).new()` per branch. A menu has no closest pair in any meaningful sense, because its values are not points in a space; asking which two of SINE_WAVE, LANGTONS_ANT and PRIM_MST are nearest is asking which two branches of a switch statement are nearest. That is a claim about the corpus's own method and this bench is where it is made.

FIVE THINGS THE CODE SAID THAT THE BRIEF DID NOT.

  1. RULE30, RULE110 AND RULE90 ARE ONE ALGORITHM AT THREE VALUES OF A PARAMETER, and grid2d's factory says so in three consecutive lines - `cartridge_rule_1d.gd.new(30)`, `.new(110)`, `.new(90)`. That cartridge's entire state is `var rule_number: int = 30`, and its step() is one line of bit arithmetic on it. Meanwhile ca_bridge declares an axis literally named `rule` with values [30, 90, 110, 250], and wave 16's rule_bench was built on that family with `rule: [30, 90, 110, 250, 218]`. THE CORPUS DECLARES ONE THING UNDER TWO AXIS NAMES, and the honest name is the one on the other artifact. The brief asked whether these are the same as ca_bridge's `rule` values: they are, three of the four, and it is worse than a coincidence of numbers - grid2d spent three MENU ENTRIES on what ca_bridge correctly spends one AXIS on.

  2. SLOW IS THE SAME SHAPE AGAIN, and sharper than the brief guessed. The brief said SLOW is a speed. cartridge_slow.gd is a real rule - `grid[i] = (grid[i] + 1) % 8` over a diagonal `(x + y) % 8` init - and its own header says "Same F_order rule as disco; the array reads as different BECAUSE THE RATE CHANGES", with "only the step interval differs (set in map config)". So SLOW and DISCO are ONE rule at two tempos; the tempo is not in the enum at all, it arrives from the map; and in the code the two values differ by SAT 0.4 against 0.7 and VAL 0.7 against 0.95. A palette and a clock, declared as two algorithms. Declined, and the rule cited is the one that costs a sweep: a rate is invisible to a still.

  3. RANDOM IS NOT AN ALGORITHM AND THE FILE SAYS SO. cartridge_random.gd is `grid[i] = randi() % 8` for every cell every step; its header calls it "the 'antithesis' cartridge - same hardware, no memory" and says the values "are unrelated to anything else". It is the absence of a rule sitting in the list of rules, and it is unseeded, so it cannot be photographed twice. Declined on both counts.

  4. AND POINT 3 GENERALISES, WHICH IS WHY THIS BENCH HAD TO REBUILD RATHER THAN PHOTOGRAPH. cartridge_game_of_life seeds with bare `randf()`, cartridge_bfs lays its walls with bare `randf()`, cartridge_dfs_maze picks its neighbour with bare `randi()`, cartridge_logistic_map draws `randf_range(0.1, 0.9)` per column per iteration, cartridge_bell_curve draws six `randf()` per sample. NOT ONE of the three members declares a seed anywhere, and all three step under `_process` against a `step_interval`. Most values of this axis are a different picture on every boot AND at every shutter. That is the reason the axis has never been swept and the reason cohort_bench could inherit a family seed while this bench cannot.

  5. A THIRTEENTH VALUE EXISTS AND NO TOOL IN THE CHAIN CAN SEE IT. grid2d's enum has THIRTEEN members. DISCO is the eleventh, it has a cartridge file, a factory branch, and a key in both of the file's alias tables. The registry declares twelve. `python tools/check_dna_declarations.py` reports `grid2d.algorithm ok`. The cause: `code_values()` reads a typed enum by splitting its body on commas, and the comment line above DISCO contains one - "# array_tutorial sequence cartridges - same array, three cadences" - so DISCO is swallowed into the token "three cadences\n\tDISCO", which fails the identifier check and is dropped. Reproduced directly: `code_values(src, 'algorithm')` returns 12 names while `'DISCO' in src` is true. THE DERIVING TOOL AND THE GATE ARE THE SAME PARSER, so they agree with each other and disagree with the code, and the one gate built to catch declaration drift is blind to this class of it. That is a fault in the harness rather than in grid2d, and it is the largest single thing this pass found.

ALGORITHM, eight values, spanning all three members and all three kinds, with the members' own spellings kept character for character.

  RULE30 (grid2d) - Wolfram elementary rule 30 from a single centre cell on a wrapped 33-cell line, 33 generations down the panel. A full symmetric triangle and the densest of the three: 437 of 1089 lit, 214 left of centre against 205 right. The chaotic one, and the flattering default.
  RULE110 (grid2d) - rule 110, the same single cell. GROWS LEFT ONLY: from a lone 1, neighbourhood 001 gives 1 and 100 gives 0, so the light cone opens to the left and stands still on the right. 228 lit in the left half against 89 in the right, 350 total, and its envelope is half a triangle where 30's and 90's are full ones. THE ENVELOPE, NOT THE INTERIOR, IS WHAT SEPARATES IT.
  RULE90 (grid2d) - rule 90, the XOR rule: the Sierpinski gasket. Symmetric exactly like 30 (122 left, 122 right) and sparse exactly where 30 is dense - 245 lit against 437 inside the same triangular support. So 30 and 90 share an envelope and differ inside; 30 and 110 share a density and differ in envelope. Whole-frame Hamming over 1089 cells: 30 vs 110 differ in 403, 30 vs 90 in 380, 110 vs 90 in 377.
  BFS_FLOOD (grid2d) - breadth-first flood from the centre over the grid's own 4-neighbour adjacency, at cartridge_bfs.gd's own 25 percent wall density with its own 5x5 clearing around the source. 260 walls, 823 of the 829 open cells reachable, maximum depth 43. The ordering quantity is HOP COUNT, and the contours it draws are diamonds because every edge costs the same.
  DFS_MAZE (grid2d) - depth-first traversal of the SAME graph, next neighbour drawn from a seeded generator. The ordering quantity is DISCOVERY INDEX, 0 to 822, because DEPTH-FIRST HAS NO METRIC TO MINIMISE. That is not a defect in the rendering, it is the difference between this value and the other two, and it is why `search` can be a kind and cannot be a metric: two of its three members compute a distance and the third computes only an order. The relief is a snaking ribbon where the other two are cones.
  DIJKSTRA (grid3d) - shortest path over the SAME graph with a weight in [0.5, 1.5] on every edge, settled greedily. Maximum distance 44.202 against BFS's 43. SET EVERY WEIGHT TO 1.0 AND THIS VALUE IS BFS_FLOOD, exactly and not approximately. It is the pre-registered closest pair and it is drawn from two DIFFERENT members' menus - which is the whole argument in one pair of tiles.
  SINE_WAVE (profile) - sin(2 tau x) at cartridge_sine_wave.gd's own `_frequency = 2.0`, with its `delta_time * _phase_speed` term pinned at zero. Two full cycles across the panel, crest touching level 0 and level 32, 561 filled cells. THE PIN IS NOT A SIMPLIFICATION: in the member the phase is a function of elapsed clock, so a still of the shipped cartridge is a fact about the shutter.
  LOGISTIC_MAP (profile) - r swept 2.5 to 4.0 across the 33 columns, 200 draws per column, 100 settling iterations each, combined by the cartridge's own running mean `buf = lerpf(buf, x, 1 / k)`. THE BIFURCATION CARTRIDGE DRAWS NO BIFURCATION. Averaging an attractor collapses it: past r = 3 the orbit is a 2-cycle whose mean is (r + 1) / 2r, a smooth curve, so the fan never appears. Replica: the 33 columns span 0.5195 to 0.6757, which is 0.156 of the declared [0, 1] y-range and six of thirty-three levels - a nearly flat line, 699 filled cells. The cartridge's own comment inside step() reads "Actually: for bifurcation diagram, each column should show the last N values" and then averages anyway. This is the same shape of fault cohort_bench found three times in its own family: the artifact promises the thing and draws its own substitute.

KIND, three values, AND IT IS A PARTITION OF THE OTHER AXIS RATHER THAN A SECOND FREE DIMENSION. It names what the panel's two directions MEAN, which is the only thing that makes two values comparable at all.

  automaton - a local rule iterated. i is the cell, j is the generation, row 0 is the initial condition at the top of the panel. Six of grid2d's twelve values are this kind (GAME_OF_LIFE, SEEDS, BRIANS_BRAIN, RULE30, RULE110, RULE90, plus WIRE_WORLD and LANGTONS_ANT depending on how strictly one reads 'local rule'). Note that the three built here share ONE `initialize()` because they are one cartridge, so the initial row belongs to the kind and not to any value - which is exactly why the bare automaton cell is that row and nothing under it.
  search - a traversal of a graph. i and j are space, and the grid's own 4-neighbour adjacency IS the graph. Two of grid2d's twelve and six of grid3d's eight. Band and relief carry the quantity the traversal orders by, normalised to its own maximum and quantised into four bands, so the picture is a set of iso-contours.
  signal - a function of one variable sampled. i is the variable, j is the value, quantised to 33 levels and filled from the baseline up to the crest. ALL SIXTEEN of profile's values are this kind and nothing else is.

THAT COUNT IS THE ARGUMENT IN ONE LINE. The three members are not three widgets that happen to share a word; they are three widgets each of which is ALMOST ENTIRELY ONE KIND. profile is sixteen signals. grid3d is six searches, one graph generator (RANDOM_GRAPH) and one field (ENTROPY_FIELD). grid2d is the only mixed one, and its mixture is six automata, two searches, and four things that are not algorithms at all (SLOW, DISCO, RANDOM, and arguably WIRE_WORLD's circuit substrate). A `kind` axis would have had three values and made the family comparable; `algorithm` has thirty-six and makes it a switch.

BECAUSE `kind` PARTITIONS `algorithm`, MOST CELLS ARE UNDEFINED, AND THE EMPTINESS IS DRAWN RATHER THAN HIDDEN. 8 of the 24 cells are native. The other 16 render the KIND'S BARE SUBSTRATE and never consult the algorithm at all: the spacetime panel with its initial row and no rule; the graph with its 260 walls and its source and nobody having walked it; the two axes with no function on them. So all five foreign cells in the automaton column are one image, all five in search are one image, all six in signal are one image - 16 frames, 3 pictures, pre-registered below as designed nulls. The alternative, inventing a rendering for a rule that is not defined on a graph, would have produced sixteen plausible-looking tiles about nothing, which is the exact failure mode this programme exists to catch.

HOW THE SHEET IS PROTECTED FROM THE COLOUR TRAP. The critic measures luminance by default and has a separate per-channel rescue, so a pair separated only by hue at constant brightness reads as a twin in greyscale. The full Rec.709 ladder is panel 0.180, off 0.292, corner stud 0.411, then the value ramp at 0.525, 0.643, 0.757, 0.876. NO TWO STEPS ARE CLOSER THAN 0.112, and the ramp also carries a hue arc from cool to warm so the colour rescue and the luminance reading agree rather than compete. A wall in the search kind is drawn in the PANEL's own colour at full relief - deliberately no new grey, because a wall is the substrate standing up. Value is carried by relief AND albedo at once: D_OFF 0.004, D_LO 0.008, D_BODY 0.018, D_MAX 0.034.

WHY THE FIELD STANDS VERTICAL, AND IT IS A MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN A STYLE. The sweep's canonical standpoint is yaw 0.62, pitch -0.26, which is an elevation of 14.90 degrees. On a HORIZONTAL 33 x 33 field at that pitch a 0.090 m post hides 0.338 m of grid behind it - 13.3 cells - so eleven of every twelve rows would be a photograph of the front row's backs, and the horizontal top face is only 29.8 percent of the subject box. On a VERTICAL panel the same relief hides 0.024 m sideways, 0.95 of one cell, and the face fills 82.1 percent of the subject box. Both numbers were computed from the capturer's own constants BEFORE the geometry was written. This is the corpus's own 'the artifact's furniture is in front of its marks' trap, caught by arithmetic instead of by a wasted sweep.

THE THESIS SOMEONE COULD DISAGREE WITH: a DNA axis must be a dimension, and an axis whose values are the branches of a dispatch table is a category error that the whole promotion apparatus - the deriving tool, the gate, the sweep, the critic - will process without objecting once. THE DISAGREEMENT AVAILABLE, and it is fair: a reader can say that `algorithm` is exactly the right axis for a SUBSTRATE, whose entire purpose is to be a reusable body that different content is loaded into, and that the cartridge system is a virtue rather than a fault - grid2d's README calls the substrate the hardware and the cartridge the choice. The answer is that this is precisely the case for the axis being called `cartridge` or `kind` rather than `algorithm`, and for the axis carrying what varies rather than what is plugged in: because it is called `algorithm` and holds thirty-six unrelated words, the corpus now declares Wolfram's rule number twice under two different names, cannot see that two of its members list the same traversal, and has one enum member no tool in the chain can read.

predicted_degeneracy.pair: BFS_FLOOD against DIJKSTRA, in the search kind
predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic:
THE CONTEXT IS THE `search` COLUMN AND THE RANKING IS COMPUTED INSIDE IT: three pairs, BFS_FLOOD-DIJKSTRA 9.70, BFS_FLOOD-DFS_MAZE 35.64, DIJKSTRA-DFS_MAZE 36.00. The two DFS pairs are far because that value has no metric at all - its field is a discovery index running 0 to 822 along a snaking stack order, so its bands bear no relation to distance from the source and roughly half the panel changes band. The named pair changes only where a wobble in the weights pushes a cell across a contour.

WHY THAT PAIR IS THE FLOOR OF THE SHEET, AND IT IS BY CONSTRUCTION. BFS_FLOOD and DIJKSTRA are handed THE SAME OBJECT: the same 1089 cells, the same 260 walls out of one seeded draw, the same source, the same 823 reachable cells, the same normalisation by their own maximum. Dijkstra with every edge weight set to 1.0 IS breadth-first search - that is a theorem, not a resemblance - and the weights here are drawn U(0.5, 1.5), whose mean is exactly 1.0. So the two fields differ only by the accumulated deviation of a sum of d unit-mean draws, which has standard deviation 0.2887 * sqrt(d); at the deepest cells (d = 43) that is 1.89 against a maximum of 43, about 4.4 percent of full scale. Verified on the replica: max depth 43 against max distance 44.202, and the normalised per-cell difference has mean 0.0512 and maximum 0.1521.

THE NUMBER, AND IT IS SET BY THE BAND STEP RATHER THAN BY THE FIELDS. The AABB is 0.96 x 0.96 x 0.058, diagonal 1.35888. The critic crops to the union of the two frames' subject boxes - identical here, because the stage is - and resizes to 160 x 160 = 25600 px. At yaw 0.62 / pitch -0.26 the screen basis is x-hat -> (0.8139, -0.1494), y-hat -> (0, 0.9664), z-hat -> (-0.5810, -0.2093), so the subject box is 0.96*0.8139 + 0.058*0.5810 = 0.8150 m wide by 0.96*0.1494 + 0.96*0.9664 + 0.058*0.2093 = 1.0833 m tall = 0.8829 m2, and the panel face projects at 0.9216 * 0.78652 = 0.7249 m2, which is 82.1 percent of the box. The 0.84 m field is 0.7056/0.9216 of that, so 16092 of the 25600 px, and 1089 cells at 14.78 px each. THE HOTTEST 5 PERCENT IS 1280 px = 86.6 CELLS. Replica: 160 of the 823 reached cells cross a band boundary between the two fields - 1.85x the window - SO THE WINDOW FILLS ENTIRELY WITH BAND-CROSSERS AND THE MEASURED NUMBER IS THE BAND STEP, NOT THE FIELD DIFFERENCE. The four ramp luminances are 0.525, 0.643, 0.757, 0.876; the steps are 0.118, 0.114, 0.119, and the top-87 mean |dGrey| is 0.1150. The relief term adds a mean |dDepth| of 0.00222 m out of 0.034 against a 0.6 albedo contrast at 0.30 weighting = 0.0118. Total 0.1268 of full scale; applying the lighting-and-tonemap compression the substance_room replica measured at 0.77 gives 9.76. Registered at 9.7.

THE TWO WAYS THIS CAN BE WRONG, AND BOTH ARE INFORMATIVE. (a) BELOW 9.7: the window has stopped filling, which means fewer than 87 cells cross a band - the replica has 160, so Godot's PCG32 would have to draw a much tighter weight set than Python's Mersenne Twister did. That would be a fact about the draw, and the fix is more bands, not a new axis. Also check tools/check_dna_declarations.py and _rejects.json first, per the standing rule. (b) ABOVE ABOUT 13: more than one band step is being crossed in the hot window, which the arithmetic above says cannot happen from the weight draw alone - so something else is moving, most likely the normalisation denominator (if Dijkstra's maximum lands on a different cell than BFS's, the whole field rescales) or a shadow term the flat-shaded replica cannot see. NOTE THAT THE USUAL 1.5x-to-6.7x UNDER-READ SHOULD NOT APPLY HERE: those factors come from shadows, AO and antialiasing adding contrast the replica has no model for, and this prediction is CAPPED by a quantisation the renderer cannot widen. A result of 30 percent would falsify the band mechanism outright, which is the most useful thing this prediction can do.

AND A SECOND PRE-REGISTERED CLAIM, ABOUT THE INSTRUMENT RATHER THAN THE DESIGN: IN THE `automaton` KIND THE CRITIC'S STATISTIC CANNOT RANK ANYTHING. All three cells are binary - a lit cell is 0.876 at D_MAX, an unlit one 0.292 at D_OFF - and all three pairs differ in far more than 87 cells (403, 380, 377 out of 1089). So the hot-5 percent window fills entirely with full-contrast flips and ALL THREE PAIRS RETURN THE SAME NUMBER, predicted 59.2, to within render noise. If the sweep reports three different automaton numbers spread by more than about 2 points, the window is not filling and the crop is smaller than this arithmetic assumes. The honest ranking in that kind is whole-frame Hamming, where RULE110-RULE90 (377) is closest and RULE30-RULE110 (403) is furthest - and that ordering is invisible to the published headline, which is worth knowing about every binary-state axis in the corpus.

designed_nulls.why: IDENTICAL BY CONSTRUCTION AND IT IS THE THESIS, not a spare check. Neither cell is defined: a breadth-first flood and a sine wave are both undefined on a spacetime diagram of a 1-D line, so `_build_field` never consults the algorithm and renders the kind's bare substrate - the initial row, one lit cell at the top centre, and nothing under it. THE FIVE FOREIGN CELLS IN THIS COLUMN ARE ONE IMAGE: BFS_FLOOD, DFS_MAZE, DIJKSTRA, SINE_WAVE and LOGISTIC_MAP at kind=automaton are the same 1089 boxes, vertex for vertex. Predicted 0.00 percent focus and 0.00 percent frame. Anything above 0.3 percent is render noise; anything above 2 percent means `_is_native()` is reading something it must not, and nothing else in the sheet can be believed until it is found. THE CONTRAST THAT MUST HOLD ALONGSIDE IT: each of RULE30, RULE110 and RULE90 against this same bare cell should measure about 59, because 245 to 437 cells flip full contrast - a null that held there too would mean the automaton branch never ran.

The same identity in the search column, and it is the one that also proves the graph belongs to the KIND. Both cells render the bare graph: 260 walls proud at D_MAX in the panel's own colour, 829 open cells at D_OFF, and the source alone at D_LO in band 0. Nobody has walked it. All five foreign cells here - RULE30, RULE110, RULE90, SINE_WAVE, LOGISTIC_MAP at kind=search - are that one image. Predicted 0.00 percent. IF THIS PAIR IS NOT ZERO, the wall draw is being reseeded per cell, which would also silently invalidate the pre-registered BFS_FLOOD-against-DIJKSTRA pair, because that pair's entire claim is that the two searches are handed the same graph.

The third and largest identity group: SIX foreign cells in the signal column - RULE30, RULE110, RULE90, BFS_FLOOD, DFS_MAZE and DIJKSTRA - all rendering the two axes with no function on them, the baseline at level 16 across all 33 columns and the value axis up column 0, at D_BODY in band 1. Predicted 0.00 percent. Together the three nulls account for 16 of the sheet's 24 frames collapsing to 3 images, which is not a defect in the sheet: IT IS THE MEASUREMENT. A cross product that is two thirds empty is what a partition looks like when it is drawn against the thing it partitions, and no other pair of axes in the corpus has ever been declared this way.

dna.designed_nulls_why: THREE NULLS, ONE FACT, AND IT IS THE ARGUMENT RATHER THAN A CHECK ON IT. `kind` partitions `algorithm` instead of crossing it, so two thirds of the cross product is undefined, and the only honest rendering of an undefined cell is the substrate with nothing applied. That makes 16 of 24 frames into 3 images and the identities are exact rather than approximate - the same code path, the same arguments, the same meshes. THE TEMPTING FOURTH NULL WAS REFUSED: BFS_FLOOD against DIJKSTRA with the weights pinned to 1.0 would be an exact identity too, and a far more elegant one, but pinning them would delete the only live comparison in the search column and turn the pre-registered closest pair into a null. The weights stay drawn, the pair stays live at a predicted 9.7 percent, and the theorem that they coincide at unit weight is stated in the note instead of photographed. Note also what is NOT registered here: no pair of NATIVE cells is predicted identical anywhere in this sheet, because every native cell runs a different computation on the same body, and a family whose members really did overlap would have produced one - which is the difference between this family and cohort_bench's.
dna.fixture_why: The bench can stand the eight native cells in a row (layout=ladder, 1.10 m pitch, about 7.7 m wide) but the SWEEP must see one at a time: capture_config_sweep unions the AABB across a spec's variants, so an eight-wide row in the same spec would frame every single cell against nearly eight metres and photograph the 0.019 m cells as dust. `layout` is an export and not an axis, it ships at `single`, and the fixture is a belt over braces. WHAT IS NOT FIXTURED, AND WHY NOTHING NEEDS TO BE: there is no clock and no unseeded draw here. Every random quantity comes from a RandomNumberGenerator seeded off RNG_SEED 20260816 - the walls from the seed itself, the edge weights from seed + 7717, the depth-first neighbour choice from seed + 4242, the logistic map's initial conditions from seed + 991. There is no _process, no Timer, no tween, no FastNoiseLite and deliberately no NoiseTexture2D, which bakes on a worker thread and would let the shutter catch an unbaked map. That matters more here than usual because THE SOURCES ARE THE OPPOSITE OF QUIET: all three step under _process against a step_interval, all three ship auto_play true, and their cartridges call bare randf()/randi() with no seed anywhere in any of the three files. Every one of them would have to refuse its own time-domain exports as axes; this bench has none to refuse.
dna.kin: The three sources are the kin, and the relation is unusual because this bench shares their AXIS NAME and almost none of their values - the opposite of cohort_bench, which shared five words out of five. grid2d is a horizontal petri dish of MultiMesh cells whose README calls the substrate the hardware and the cartridge the choice; grid3d is a volumetric node-and-edge cloud in a 2.0 x 1.5 x 2.0 m box; profile is a ribbon-strip curve over a grid background. Three bodies, three vocabularies, one word. A room holding this bench beside any one of the three is saying: here are eight of your thirty-six on one body, and here is what your word was hiding. A room holding it beside ca_bridge or beside wave 16's rule_bench is making the sharper point, because those two declare an axis called `rule` whose values [30, 90, 110, 250] are three of grid2d's twelve menu entries - the same parameter, correctly named on one artifact and expanded into a menu on another. THE SECOND KIN GROUP IS THE ONE-SCENE-MANY-NAMES PATTERN, and this family carries the corpus's largest instance of it: grid2d has ten sibling tokens (grid2d_life, grid2d_seeds, grid2d_brians_brain, grid2d_rule30, grid2d_rule110, grid2d_rule90, grid2d_bfs, grid2d_dfs_maze, grid2d_wireworld, grid2d_langtons_ant), grid3d has eight and profile has sixteen, every one of them pointing at its parent's scene and resolving its value from `artifact_lookup_name`. So the dispatch table is registered TWICE - once as an axis with N values and once as N tokens each pinning one value - and the 34 sibling tokens are the family's real placements.
declines: GAME_OF_LIFE, and it is the decline that shaped the whole subset. Conway's Life is a 2-D automaton, so BOTH of its grid directions are space, while the three elementary rules make one direction space and the other TIME. Building them in the same kind would have required the substrate to mean two different things inside one kind, which destroys the only property that makes `kind` worth having. So the automaton kind here is the 1-D reading, and the fact that grid2d's twelve values contain both readings under one word - five 2-D automata and one 1-D one wearing three names - is written down rather than papered over. SEEDS, BRIANS_BRAIN, WIRE_WORLD and LANGTONS_ANT are declined for the same reason, and LANGTONS_ANT additionally because its picture is a single moving head on an otherwise static field, which is a rate rather than a state.

SLOW AND RANDOM, declined on the brief's own rule and on the code's evidence. The rule is that a rate, a duration or a decay is invisible to a still. RANDOM is `randi() % 8` on every cell every step from the GLOBAL generator - not an algorithm (its own header calls it 'the antithesis cartridge - same hardware, no memory') and not reproducible (unseeded, so two boots are two pictures). SLOW is subtler than the brief guessed and is declined for a different reason than the brief gave: it is not a speed, it is a real rule, `grid[i] = (grid[i] + 1) % 8`, which its own header says is IDENTICAL to DISCO's - the two values differ by a step_interval that arrives from the map and by SAT/VAL palette constants. One rule, two menu entries, and the only difference a still could show is the palette.

DISCO, declined because it cannot be declared. It is grid2d's eleventh enum member with a real cartridge and a real factory branch, and `tools/check_dna_declarations.py` cannot see it - the comment above it contains a comma and the enum body is split on commas. Including it here would have been fine (this artifact uses @export_enum, not a typed enum) but it would have quietly hidden the harness bug behind a working example. The bug is reported in `note` instead, with the reproduction.

THE MEMBERS' TYPED-ENUM DECLARATION FORM. All three sources declare `enum Algorithm {...}` plus `@export var algorithm: Algorithm`, which `code_values()` reads as 'typed enum' and returns MEMBER NAMES for, while the property is an int at runtime and capture_config_sweep converts at the moment of setting. This bench uses `@export_enum("RULE30", ...) var algorithm: String` instead, so the property IS the declared string, `Object.set()` cannot be silently refused for a type mismatch, and cabinet_sweep's `coerce()` - which numericises anything that parses as a number and cost tier_terrarium ten tiles - has nothing to numericise, because no value here parses as a number. Verified after writing: `apply_dna_block.py --token=algorithm_menu --axes=algorithm,kind` derives all eight SHOUTY_CASE spellings and all three lower-case ones character for character, underscores and capitals intact, and `check_dna_declarations.py` returns ok for both axes.

THE MEMBERS' ORIENTATION. grid2d lays its cells in the x/z plane on a horizontal base plate and grid3d fills a volume; only profile is a standing screen. A horizontal 33 x 33 field at the sweep's own standpoint - elevation 14.90 degrees - self-occludes catastrophically: a 0.090 m post hides 0.338 m of grid behind it, 13.3 cells, and the horizontal top face is 29.8 percent of the subject box. The field is stood VERTICAL, where the same relief hides 0.95 of one cell and the face fills 82.1 percent. Both figures were computed from capture_config_sweep's own YAW, PITCH, FOV and PAD constants before the geometry was written. This is a deviation from two of the three members and it is the reason the sheet is legible.

DFS_MAZE AS A MAZE. cartridge_dfs_maze.gd is a recursive-backtracker maze GENERATOR: it carves corridors between odd-coordinate cells and its walls are what it did not carve. Drawing that would have put a maze beside two flood cones, which are not comparable pictures, and the whole bench is about making a menu's entries commensurable. So the value is drawn as the DFS DISCOVERY ORDER over the same graph the other two searches walk - the maze is what depth-first LEAVES BEHIND, the order is what depth-first DOES. The decline is recorded rather than buried because it is a real change to what the member's value looks like, and because the resulting picture - a snaking ribbon against two cones - is the honest statement that this value has no metric while the other two do.

DIJKSTRA ON GRID3D'S OWN GRAPH. That member builds 20 randomly-placed nodes in a 2.0 x 1.5 x 2.0 m box and connects them by proximity; running the value there would have made the search kind's three cells incomparable again, which is the fault being diagnosed. The grid's 4-neighbour adjacency is used instead, and the choice is not arbitrary: A GRID IS A GRAPH BUT AN ARBITRARY GRAPH IS NOT A GRID, so the grid substrate can host six of grid3d's eight values while grid3d's substrate can host none of grid2d's twelve. The two members' menus are not even symmetric, which is one more thing the shared axis name conceals.

KRUSKAL_MST, PRIM_MST, FORCE_DIRECTED, RANDOM_GRAPH and ENTROPY_FIELD. The two MSTs are not traversals from a source - they build a spanning forest, so their picture is a set of EDGES and this substrate draws cells rather than edges; adding an edge layer would have made the search kind's rendering depend on which value was picked, which is the framing fault the corner studs exist to prevent. FORCE_DIRECTED is an iterative layout whose answer is a fact about how many steps have elapsed. RANDOM_GRAPH is a generator, not an algorithm - the same category error as grid2d's RANDOM, in the other member. ENTROPY_FIELD is a scalar field and would have fitted, and was left out only because the search kind already had three values and the maximum was eight.

THE OTHER FOURTEEN PROFILE VALUES. SQUARE_WAVE, SAW_WAVE and TRIANGLE_WAVE are three lines of arithmetic each and would have made the signal kind four near-identical tiles - a cheap closest pair, and a less interesting one than the search kind's. BELL_CURVE and NOISE_1D and NOISE_OCTAVES and RANDOM_WALK and BROWNIAN_BRIDGE all draw from the unseeded global generator. DAMPED_OSCILLATION, SPRING_MASS and GRADIENT_DESCENT are time-domain: their whole content is what happens as the clock runs, so a still of any of them is a fact about the shutter. LISSAJOUS_1D, FOURIER_SERIES and BEAT_FREQUENCIES would each have worked. Two were taken - the family's default (SINE_WAVE) and the one carrying a finding (LOGISTIC_MAP) - and the rest are named here so the subset is a choice on the record rather than a silence.

THE MEMBERS' SCALE AND SAMPLE COUNTS. profile ships `sample_count: int = 256`, grid2d ships 48 x 48 with cartridges overriding to 64 rows, grid3d ships 20 nodes. Everything here is rebuilt at 33 x 33 with the RATIOS preserved and named - r swept 2.5 to 4.0, 200 iterations at 100 settle, frequency 2.0, wall density 0.25, the 5x5 source clearing, depth-first's own stack discipline - so the arithmetic is checkable against the sources even though not one absolute count is shared with them. 33 is odd because an elementary automaton's initial condition is a single cell at the exact centre and an even width has none.

WRAPPING THE `algorithm` DECLARATION, which is the SECOND harness finding of this pass and cost one gate run to find. `@export_enum(...)` with eight values does not fit a line, so it was written wrapped - and check_dna_declarations returned `algorithm_menu.algorithm NO EXPORT ... but there is no such export` WHILE PRINTING THE EIGHT VALUES IT HAD JUST READ FROM THAT DECLARATION. The two halves of the same tool disagree about the same line: `has_export()` and `export_default()` match with `@export[^\n]*\bvar\s+<axis>\b`, which forbids a newline between the annotation and the `var`, while `code_values()` reads the list with `@export_enum\(([^)]*)\)`, whose negated character class DOES match newlines. So a wrapped declaration derives correctly, gates as broken, and its `default` reads as None. The line here is 143 characters and carries a comment saying it must not be wrapped. Combined with the DISCO fault in `note`, both of this pass's harness findings are in the same file and both are the same shape: A REGEX THAT ASSUMES A LINE. Neither is a fault in any artifact.

ANIMATION, AND EVERY RATE, PHASE AND TEMPO. All three members ship `step_interval` and `auto_play`, all three step under `_process`, and two of the three let a cartridge override the interval (`get_preferred_interval`). Not one of those is an axis here and not one could be: this bench's whole figure is built synchronously inside _ready from arithmetic on seeded generators. That is not a stylistic preference. It is the reason the family's own axis has never been photographed, and the reason SINE_WAVE's phase had to be pinned at zero before it could be drawn at all.
dna.sweep_note: THE FULL SHEET NEEDS --max=24 AND THE COST OF GETTING IT WRONG IS THE WHOLE ARGUMENT. `algorithm` is declared first and is never trimmed; `kind` is second, and build_dna_gallery trims the LATER axis from the tail until the cross product fits its cap. At the default --max=9 the 8 x 3 sheet renders as 8 x 1 = `automaton` only, which deletes both other kinds, the pre-registered closest pair (both its members are search values), two of the three designed nulls, and every trace of the partition - and leaves a finished-looking strip of eight tiles in which five are the identical bare substrate and nothing explains why. At --max=16 it renders 8 x 2 = automaton and search, which keeps the prediction and two nulls and deletes the signal column, so LOGISTIC_MAP and SINE_WAVE would appear only as bare cells. Only 24 carries the experiment.
